title.narrative: Counselling and mental health support for Caritas Bangladesh staff

description.narrative: Caritas Bangladesh (CB) has identified a need for its staff to receive counselling and mental health support. Staff often face high levels of emotional and psychological stress due to the nature of the organisation's work. The Innovation for Wellbeing Foundation (IWF) has put together a comprehensive programme focusing on counselling and mental health capacity building tailored to the needs of the employees of CB. 142 staff members have signed up for individual counselling sessions. These staff members will be assessed to ascertain their mental health status. Individuals will be prioritised for individual counselling depending on the severity of their mental health status; it is likely that not all the 142 staff will require individual counselling. During the assessments, common issues will be identified to be looked at in group counselling sessions i.e. stress management, conflict management, and non-violent communication. Training workshops will be held for managers and supervisors to ensure they understand how to deal with the mental health state of the employees that are receiving counselling. They will be trained on mental health first aid, stress management, conflict resolution and difficult conversations so that they know how to identify stress and burnout symptoms. Management level will also be supported to identify gaps and assist in integrating mental health services at policy and practice level. This grant will run for two years. CAFOD will discuss with CB and IWF regarding more sustainable solutions to providing counselling support to staff after December 2026 and how this can be factored into CB organisational support to staff. The current budget may reduce as not all 142 staff will need individual counselling and some may have group counselling or other support depending on need.
